quickAnswerTitle: Alabama School Calendars Are Set by Local Boards
quickAnswer: Alabama does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. State law requires each local board of education to establish its academic calendar and provide at least 180 full instructional days or no fewer than 1,080 instructional hours. Across the five reviewed 2026–27 systems, first student days range from August 5 in Madison County to August 12 in Jefferson County. Scheduled last days range from May 25 in Montgomery to June 10 in Birmingham.
about:
Alabama's statewide requirements do not create one shared first day, holiday schedule, or last day for every public school. Section 16-13-231 of the Code of Alabama directs each local board of education to establish an annual academic calendar. The same section permits a minimum term measured as 180 full instructional days or the hourly equivalent of at least 1,080 instructional hours. Families therefore need the calendar published by their assigned district.

The current MySchoolDates Alabama collection includes Birmingham City Schools, Jefferson County Schools, Madison County School System, Mobile County Public Schools, and Montgomery Public Schools. Their 2026–27 first days span August 5–12, while their scheduled last days span May 25–June 10. Even districts that open on the same date do not share every break, e-learning date, staff day, or end date.

The district pages preserve distinctions a statewide date list would erase. Birmingham publishes fall and spring intersessions; Jefferson County lists E-Learning and high-school Opportunity Days; Madison County separates E-Learning, half-days, and a Weather Day closure; Mobile County identifies Distance Learning and a Mardi Gras-related break; Montgomery publishes Asynchronous Learning Days and a separate Vacation Planner.
calendarRulesDescription: Alabama establishes the instructional minimum, while local boards adopt the dates and calendar categories families follow.

calendarRules.label: Local boards establish annual calendars
calendarRules.description: Alabama law assigns the local board of education responsibility for establishing the academic school calendar each year. First days, breaks, staff days, and last days therefore vary by district.

calendarRules.label: The minimum can be measured in days or hours
calendarRules.description: A local board must provide at least 180 full instructional days or the hourly equivalent of no fewer than 1,080 instructional hours. A printed district day total should be read together with the district's schedule and state hour option.

calendarRules.label: A scholastic day is generally six teaching hours
calendarRules.description: Section 16-1-1 defines a scholastic day as at least six hours of actual teaching, excluding recesses or intermissions, unless the local county or city board orders otherwise.

calendarRules.label: Calendar categories are not interchangeable
calendarRules.description: District PDFs may distinguish campus days, virtual or Distance Learning Days, teacher workdays, professional development, and holidays. Families should preserve the published label instead of treating every nonstandard date as a holiday.

calendarRules.label: Emergency changes remain local
calendarRules.description: When extreme circumstances cancel instruction, a local board may seek state approval for a plan that adjusts the calendar or extends teaching time on specified days. District alerts remain the source for actual changes.

stateSections.label: The State Minimum and District Day Counts Are Different Measures
stateSections.content: Alabama law permits the minimum term to be measured as 180 full instructional days or an hourly equivalent of at least 1,080 instructional hours. Montgomery prints 180 student days, and a review of Madison County's color grid also produces 180 instructional dates. Mobile County's PDF instead prints 176 student days, including two Distance Learning Days. MySchoolDates preserves the source's stated or visibly derived count but does not reconstruct daily instructional minutes or assume that every district uses the same accounting method.

stateSections.label: E-Learning, Intersessions, and Mardi Gras Remain Local
stateSections.content: The five reviewed calendars use different labels for nonstandard student dates. Birmingham schedules intersessions and e-Learning; Jefferson County uses E-Learning and Opportunity Days; Madison County uses E-Learning/Collaboration Days; Mobile County uses Distance Learning and includes a local Mardi Gras closure; Montgomery uses Asynchronous Learning Days. These labels should be read within the district that published them, not converted into statewide Alabama categories.

collectionDescription: The Alabama directory currently includes five independently reviewed district pages. Each preserves the district's own date labels, scope notes, official source files, and one-time ICS downloads.
planningTips: Start with the assigned district. Alabama's instructional minimum does not create one statewide first day, holiday schedule, or last day.
Check whether a nonstandard date is a campus closure, Distance Learning Day, teacher workday, professional-development day, or holiday before arranging childcare or transportation.
Read the first weekday after a break. A teacher workday or professional-development day may extend the time students are out beyond the printed break range.
Do not apply Mobile County's Mardi Gras closure, Birmingham's intersessions, or another system's e-learning labels to a different Alabama district without checking its official calendar.
Treat an ICS download as a one-time import. It will not automatically reflect weather decisions, school-specific events, or later district revisions.
commonHolidaysDescription: These labels appear across one or more reviewed Alabama calendars and are not presented as a universal schedule. Mardi Gras-related closures are especially local, while break ranges and staff-day sequences differ among the five systems.
verificationMethodology: Use the current Code of Alabama for statewide instructional-day, instructional-hour, and local calendar-adoption requirements.
Use each district's official calendar hub, board-approved school-year PDF, and approval notices for actual student dates.
Keep Distance Learning Days, teacher workdays, professional development, holidays, and ordinary student days in their published categories.
Do not present any reviewed district's dates, intersessions, e-learning labels, Mardi Gras closures, or day totals as statewide Alabama dates.
Count a district as reviewed only after its visible dates and source status have been checked against official district materials.

faqs.q: Does Alabama have one statewide public school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Alabama establishes the instructional framework, but each local board of education adopts its annual academic calendar. First days, breaks, staff days, Distance Learning dates, and last days can differ by district.

faqs.q: How many instructional days are required in Alabama public schools?
faqs.a: Section 16-13-231 of the Code of Alabama requires at least 180 full instructional days or the hourly equivalent of no fewer than 1,080 instructional hours. Local boards establish calendars within that framework.

faqs.q: When do the reviewed Alabama districts start school in 2026?
faqs.a: Madison County starts August 5; Birmingham City, Mobile County, and Montgomery start August 10; and Jefferson County starts August 12. These are district dates, not a statewide opening window.

faqs.q: Why does the Mobile County calendar show 176 student days?
faqs.a: The MCPSS PDF prints 176 student days, including two Distance Learning Days. Alabama law permits an hourly equivalent of at least 1,080 instructional hours instead of 180 full instructional days. The district PDF does not provide a minute-by-minute calculation, so this page preserves the published total without independently reconstructing its hours.

faqs.q: Do all Alabama schools close for Mardi Gras?
faqs.a: No statewide Mardi Gras closure is assumed. The reviewed Mobile County calendar lists February 8–12, 2027 as no-school dates for Presidents' Day and Fat Tuesday. Families in other districts should check their own board-approved calendar.

faqs.q: Can I add an Alabama school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide ICS files for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. Each file is a one-time import and will not automatically update after district revisions or emergency changes.

footerNote: Alabama calendar requirements come from current state law; student dates come from official local district calendars. Districts may revise schedules after publication, so confirm current dates before making fixed plans.
